newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES HOLD LARGELY STEADY.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES HOLD LARGELY STEADY.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term money rates were quoted little changed from their previous levels in continued liquidity on Wednesday, dealers said.

The market opened with an unsettled surplus of Z$125.6 million, with a further Z$77.4 million in maturities adding on to liquidity. The central Reserve Bank auctioned Z$85 million worth of 51-day treasury bills with an average yield of 23.08 percent.
The central bank bills were being traded on the secondary market at 22.5 percent while call money held steady at 20 percent.

NCD bills maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were trading at 24 and 23 percent (buying and selling respectively), unchanged from Tuesday and bank acceptances bills were being bought at a stable 23.5 percent and sold at 22.75 percent.
